correctness.rationale: The fan is the b=2,c=a+2 specialization of Construction 6.1; the canonical orbit-closure criterion applies over any field. The four ±1 first-coordinate rays are strict vertices, and the four remaining ray tests reduce to the balanced x=0 sections with coordinates h=y−z and g=y+z. For |k|≤1 the indicated support lines meet only the edge containing the target, preserving both edge endpoints as vertices. For k≥2 the first convex certificate with t=4/(k+2) places v₃ in the hull of its other neighbors if 2a+k+2≤0; the second places v₇ in that hull at its own ray if 2a+k+4≥0. The alternatives exhaust all a and include t=1. For the negative wing the counterpart certificates use t=4/(2−k) at h=1, or follow by the lattice map (x,y,z)↦(x,x−y,2x−z). The four variable wall degrees are 2a+k+2, 3−k, k+3 and −2a−k−4, by expressing the sum of the opposite rays in the wall basis and subtracting the coefficient sum from 2. The other fourteen are nonzero constants. Thus in the central band the only wall exclusions are (k,a)=(0,−1),(0,−2), and in the stated a=0 wings all wall degrees are nonzero despite a divisor obstruction. The secondary script was inspected but not executed.
